intro: This unit tells a very old story from India. It is called the Ramayana. You will meet Prince Rama and Princess Sita. You will meet brave Hanuman too.
Hindu families have told this story for more than 2,000 years. Many tell it at Diwali. Families in Illinois tell it too.
By the end, you can tell the story in order. You can say what keeping a promise means. You can say why every helper counts.
bigQuestion: What can a story about a promise and helpers teach us?

timeline.t: The king makes a promise to Queen Kaikeyi
Rama, Sita and Lakshmana go to the forest
Sita sees a golden deer, and Rama runs after it
Ravana carries Sita away to Lanka
Rama and Lakshmana meet Hanuman and the monkey army
Hanuman leaps across the sea and finds Sita
Everyone builds a bridge, even a little squirrel
Rama and Sita come home, and people light lamps

words.d: a very old story from India about Prince Rama and Princess Sita
saying you will surely do something
a big place with many trees and animals
something that fools you on purpose
the ten-headed king of Lanka in the Ramayana
Rama's brave helper who leads the monkey army
always staying true to a friend
the Hindu festival of lights in autumn

test.why: Rama is the prince in the Ramayana.

test.q: Why does Rama go to the forest?
Who goes with Rama to the forest?
test.why: Sita and Lakshmana go with Rama.
The golden deer is a trick to take Rama away.
Ravana, the king of Lanka, takes Sita.
Hanuman leaps across the sea and finds Sita.

test.q: What does the little squirrel teach?
test.why: Rama thanks the tiny squirrel. Every helper counts.

test.q: What do people light when Rama and Sita come home?
test.why: People light lamps to welcome Rama and Sita.

test.q: At which festival do many Hindus remember this story?
test.why: Many Hindus remember Rama and Sita's homecoming at Diwali.

test.q: How do many Hindus honor Rama and Hanuman?
test.why: Many Hindus honor Rama as a form of God and Hanuman as a model of loyal help.

write.prompt: Draw and tell. Pick one helper from the Ramayana: Lakshmana, Hanuman or the little squirrel. Draw how they helped. Tell a grown-up what the story says they did.
tips: Say "The story says..." when you tell it.
Use a word from this unit, like loyal or promise.

title: Rama, Sita and Hanuman

chapters.title: Rama, Sita and the Golden Deer
chapters.bigQuestion: Why do people keep a promise when it is hard?

story.title: The Shining Deer
story.kicker: A golden deer leaps through the forest, and Sita asks Rama to catch it.
paragraphs: The forest is green and quiet. Rama and Sita live in a small hut. Rama's brother Lakshmana lives there too. They have lived in the forest for many years.
One morning, something shines between the trees. It is a deer! Its coat is gold. Its spots look like silver. Sita smiles. "Please catch that deer for me," she says.
Rama picks up his bow. He runs after the deer. The deer runs far, far away into the trees. But this deer is not a real deer. It is a trick.
What will happen to Sita now? This very old story tells us. Families in India and in Illinois still love to tell it today.
story.think: Sita saw something beautiful and wanted it. Have you ever wanted something you saw?

lessons.title: The Ramayana
lessons.mainIdea: The Ramayana is a very old story from India.
reading: The *Ramayana* is a story from India. It is very, very old. People have told it for more than 2,000 years.
A poet named Valmiki told the story in a long poem. Today people tell it in books, songs, plays and cartoons.

words.d: a very old story from India about Prince Rama and Princess Sita

look.title: A Grandma Tells a Story
look.text: Look at the grandma on the soft couch. A small boy sits on her lap. She holds an old book with bright pictures. She points to a prince with a bow. She says, "This is Rama."
look.prompt: Who tells you stories at home? What is your favorite one?

check.q: Where does the Ramayana come from?
check.why: The Ramayana is a very old story from India.

check.q: Is the Ramayana a new story or an old story?
choices: A story from a TV show made this year
check.why: People have told the Ramayana for more than 2,000 years.

check.q: Who told the Ramayana as a long poem?
check.why: Hindus remember the poet Valmiki as the teller of the Ramayana poem.

lessons.title: Rama, Sita and Lakshmana
lessons.mainIdea: Rama, Sita and Lakshmana are the main people in the story.
reading: Rama is a prince. He is kind and brave. Sita is a princess. She is Rama's wife. She is kind and strong.
Lakshmana is Rama's brother. He stays with Rama always. Many Hindus honor Rama as a form of God. They love Sita too.

words.d: the son of a king and queen
the daughter of a king and queen, or a prince's wife

look.title: Three Friends in a Picture
look.text: Look at the picture. A prince holds a bow. His skin is painted blue. Many artists paint Rama blue. A princess in yellow stands by him. His brother stands close by.
look.prompt: Point to Rama. Point to Sita. How can you tell who is who?

check.q: Who is Rama?
check.why: In the Ramayana, Rama is a prince.

check.q: Who is Lakshmana?
check.why: Lakshmana is Rama's brother. He stays with Rama.

check.q: How do many Hindus honor Rama?
check.why: Many Hindus honor Rama as a form of God.

lessons.title: The King's Promise
lessons.mainIdea: Rama goes to the forest to keep his father's promise.
reading: Rama's father is King Dasharatha. Long ago, the king made a promise to Queen Kaikeyi. He said he would give her two wishes.
Now the queen asks for her wishes. She wants her son Bharata to be king. She wants Rama to live in the forest for fourteen years.
The king is very sad. But a promise is a promise. Rama is calm. He says, "I will go, Father."

words.d: saying you will surely do something

look.title: Rama Says Yes
look.text: Rama tells the queen he will go to the forest. He says he will do what his father promised. He is not angry.
look.cite: Retold from Valmiki's Ramayana, Ayodhya Kanda (Book 2)
look.prompt: Rama is not angry. Why do you think he says yes?

check.q: Who made the promise?
check.why: King Dasharatha, Rama's father, made a promise to Queen Kaikeyi.

check.q: How long will Rama live in the forest?
check.why: Queen Kaikeyi asks that Rama live in the forest for fourteen years.

check.q: What does Rama do?
choices: He keeps the promise and goes
check.why: Rama keeps his father's promise, even though it is hard.

lessons.title: Into the Forest
lessons.mainIdea: Sita and Lakshmana choose to go with Rama.
reading: Rama must go to the forest. Sita says, "I will go with you." Lakshmana says, "I will go too."
They leave the palace. They wear simple clothes. They walk into the big forest. They build a little hut to live in.

words.d: a big place with many trees and animals

look.title: Who Went to the Forest?
look.prompt: Count them. How many people went to the forest?

check.q: Who goes to the forest with Rama?
check.why: Sita and Lakshmana choose to go with Rama.

check.q: Where do they live in the forest?
check.why: They build a little hut in the forest.

check.q: Why does Sita go?
choices: She wants to stay with Rama
check.why: Sita wants to be with Rama, so she goes too.

lessons.title: A Deer That Is a Trick
lessons.mainIdea: The golden deer is a trick to take Rama away.
reading: Sita sees a golden deer. She asks Rama to catch it. Rama runs after the deer. Then Lakshmana goes to find Rama.
The deer was a trick. Now Sita is alone. Nobody is there to keep her safe. That was the plan.

words.d: something that fools you on purpose

look.title: Too Good to Be True
look.text: Look at the deer in the picture. Its fur shines like gold. Its spots shine like silver. No real deer looks like this.
look.prompt: What clue tells you this deer is not a real deer?

check.q: What does Sita ask Rama to do?
check.why: Sita sees the golden deer and asks Rama to catch it.

check.q: What is the golden deer really?
check.why: In the Ramayana, the golden deer is a trick.

check.q: Who is left alone at the hut?
check.why: Rama and Lakshmana go away, so Sita is left alone.

lessons.title: Ravana Takes Sita
lessons.mainIdea: Ravana, king of Lanka, carries Sita far away.
reading: Ravana is the king of Lanka. The story says he has ten heads. He comes to the hut. He carries Sita away in his flying chariot.
A brave bird named Jatayu tries to stop him. Sita drops her jewelry as a clue. Rama will need help to find her.

words.d: the ten-headed king of Lanka in the Ramayana
Ravana's kingdom across the sea

look.title: A Trail of Jewels
look.text: As Ravana flies, Sita drops her jewels to the ground below. She hopes Rama will find them.
look.cite: Retold from Valmiki's Ramayana, Aranya Kanda (Book 3) and Kishkindha Kanda (Book 4)
look.prompt: Why is dropping the jewels a smart idea?

check.q: Who carries Sita away?
check.why: Ravana, the king of Lanka, carries Sita away.

check.q: How many heads does the story give Ravana?
check.why: The Ramayana says Ravana has ten heads.

check.q: What does Sita drop as a clue?
check.why: Sita drops her jewelry so Rama can find her trail.

choices: A very old story from India
review.why: The Ramayana is a very old story from India.

review.q: Why does Rama go to the forest?
review.why: Rama keeps King Dasharatha's promise to Queen Kaikeyi.

review.q: What does Sita see in the forest?
review.why: Sita sees a shining golden deer.
Ravana is the king of Lanka.

review.q: How do many Hindus honor Rama?
review.why: Many Hindus honor Rama as a form of God.

chapters.title: Hanuman the Brave Helper
chapters.bigQuestion: How can every helper, big or small, make a difference?

story.title: The Little Squirrel
story.kicker: A little squirrel rolls in the sand and shakes it onto a bridge of stones.
paragraphs: Big monkeys carry big stones. Splash! They drop them in the sea. They are building a bridge to Lanka. Rama needs it to reach Sita.
A little squirrel watches. "I want to help too," it thinks. It runs into the water. Then it rolls and rolls in the soft sand on the beach.
The squirrel runs to the bridge. It shakes the sand off. The sand fills the gaps between the stones. It does this again and again.
Rama sees the squirrel. He smiles and gently strokes its back. Many families say this is how squirrels in India got their stripes.
story.think: The squirrel was very small. Was its help important? Why?

lessons.title: A Loyal Friend
lessons.mainIdea: Hanuman is Rama's loyal and brave helper.
reading: Rama and Lakshmana look for Sita. They meet a group of monkey people. They become friends. One of them is *Hanuman*.
Hanuman is very strong. He is also very loyal. Many Hindus honor Hanuman. They see him as a model of loyal help.

words.d: Rama's brave helper who leads the monkey army
always staying true to a friend

look.title: Hanuman at the Temple
look.text: Look at the murti in the temple. A murti is a sacred image. This one is Hanuman. He kneels with his hands together. Families bring flowers to him.
look.prompt: Hanuman's hands are together. What might that show about him?

check.q: Who is Hanuman?
check.why: Hanuman is Rama's loyal, brave helper in the Ramayana.

check.q: What does loyal mean?
choices: Always staying true to a friend
check.why: Loyal means you stay true to a friend.

check.q: How do many Hindus see Hanuman?
choices: As a model of loyal help
check.why: Many Hindus honor Hanuman as a model of loyal help.

lessons.title: The Monkey Army
lessons.mainIdea: Hanuman and the monkey army help Rama look for Sita.
reading: The monkey army wants to help Rama. They go north, south, east and west. They all look for Sita.
Hanuman goes south with his group. They come to the edge of the sea. Lanka is far across the water.

words.d: a big group that works together to protect or help

look.title: Looking Everywhere
look.prompt: How many ways did the groups go?

check.q: What does the monkey army do?
check.why: The monkey army helps Rama search for Sita.

check.q: Which way does Hanuman's group go?
check.why: Hanuman's group goes south to the sea.

check.q: What is between them and Lanka?
check.why: Lanka is across the sea.

lessons.title: The Great Leap
lessons.mainIdea: Hanuman leaps across the sea to find Sita.
reading: How can they cross the sea? Hanuman climbs a mountain. He grows very big. Then he jumps!
He flies over the waves. He lands in Lanka. He looks and looks. At last he finds Sita in a garden.

words.d: a very big jump

look.title: Hanuman Finds Sita
look.text: Hanuman finds Sita in a garden of trees. He gives her Rama's ring. Now she knows Rama is coming.
look.cite: Retold from Valmiki's Ramayana, Sundara Kanda (Book 5)
look.prompt: How do you think Sita felt when she saw the ring?

check.q: How does Hanuman cross the sea?
check.why: In the story, Hanuman makes a giant leap across the sea.

check.q: Where does Hanuman find Sita?
check.why: Hanuman finds Sita in a garden in Lanka.

check.q: What does Hanuman give Sita?
check.why: Hanuman gives Sita Rama's ring as a sign.

lessons.title: Good News for Rama
lessons.mainIdea: Hanuman brings Rama good news about Sita.
reading: Hanuman leaps back over the sea. He runs straight to Rama. "I found Sita! She is safe!" he says.
Rama is so happy. He hugs Hanuman. Now they know where Sita is. They make a plan to bring her home.

words.d: something new that you tell others

look.title: A Big Hug
look.text: Look at Rama and Hanuman. Rama hugs Hanuman close. Hanuman smiles. The other monkeys cheer and jump.
look.prompt: How does it feel when someone thanks you for helping?

check.q: What news does Hanuman bring?
check.why: Hanuman tells Rama that he found Sita.

check.q: How does Rama feel?
check.why: Rama is happy and hugs Hanuman.

check.q: What do they do next?
choices: Make a plan to bring Sita home
check.why: They make a plan to bring Sita home.

lessons.title: The Stone Bridge
lessons.mainIdea: Everyone helps build a bridge, even a tiny squirrel.
reading: The monkey army builds a bridge of stones. It goes all the way to Lanka. Big and small, they all help.
Many families tell about a little squirrel too. It carries sand. This squirrel story is a well-loved folk telling. It is not in Valmiki's poem.

words.d: a path built over water
a story families pass on by telling it

look.title: The Squirrel's Stripes
look.text: Look at a squirrel in India. It has three light stripes on its back. Families say the stripes came from Rama's fingers. He thanked the squirrel gently.
look.prompt: Why do you think families love to tell this story?

check.q: What does the army build?
check.why: The monkey army builds a stone bridge to Lanka.

check.q: What does the little squirrel carry?
check.why: In the folk telling, the squirrel carries sand.

check.q: Is the squirrel story in Valmiki's poem?
choices: Yes, it is the first page
No, it is from a TV show only
No, it is a folk telling families share
check.why: The squirrel story is a well-loved folk telling, not part of Valmiki's poem.

lessons.title: Rama and Sita Come Home
lessons.mainIdea: Rama brings Sita home, and people light lamps to welcome them.
reading: Rama and his friends cross the bridge. There is a big battle. Rama wins. Sita is free!
Rama, Sita and Lakshmana go home to Ayodhya. It is night. The people light many lamps to welcome them.

words.d: Rama's home city

look.title: A City of Lamps
look.text: Look at the city at night. Tiny lamps glow on every step. Lamps glow in every window. People wave and cheer. Rama and Sita are home.
look.prompt: Why do you think the people lit so many lamps?

check.q: Where do Rama and Sita go at the end?
check.why: Rama and Sita go home to Ayodhya.

check.q: What do the people light?
check.why: The people light many lamps to welcome Rama and Sita.

check.q: Which festival do many Hindus link to this homecoming?
check.why: Many Hindus remember Rama and Sita coming home at Diwali, the festival of lights.

lessons.title: Lamps at Diwali
lessons.mainIdea: Many Hindus remember this homecoming at Diwali.
reading: Today many Hindu families light lamps at Diwali. Diwali is the festival of lights. Many remember Rama and Sita coming home.
Families in Illinois light lamps too. They share sweets. They tell the story again. Everyone who helped is remembered.

words.d: the Hindu festival of lights in autumn

look.title: Diwali at Home
look.text: Look at the family by the door. Mom sets out little clay lamps. A boy counts them: one, two, three, all the way to twelve. Grandpa holds a box of sweets.
look.prompt: Why might a family light lamps by the door?

check.q: What is Diwali?
check.why: Diwali is the Hindu festival of lights.

check.q: What do many Hindus remember at Diwali?
check.why: Many Hindus remember Rama and Sita's return at Diwali.

check.q: Do families in Illinois celebrate Diwali?
check.why: Many Hindu families in Illinois celebrate Diwali.

review.why: Hanuman leaps across the sea to find Sita.

review.q: What does the monkey army build?
review.why: The monkey army builds a stone bridge to Lanka.

review.q: How does the little squirrel help?
choices: It carries sand to the bridge
review.why: In the folk telling, the squirrel fills the gaps with sand.

review.q: What do people do when Rama and Sita come home?
review.why: People light lamps to welcome Rama and Sita.

review.q: What is the lesson of the squirrel story?
review.why: The squirrel was small, and Rama thanked it. Every helper counts.
